review_rule: A prove2.me campaign entry counts for a board only when this file names it. Its goal theorem must state the board problem: EndStatement Q.SolvedInTime v, or the same definitions with the namespace renamed, and nothing else in its statement preamble may change the meaning. Every listed file is pinned by the sha256 of the bytes after its Formalpedia header, the same bytes that Formalpedia index-*.jsonl hashes for solutions. A link needs the same proof (lead rule 2026-10-17): the prove2.me entry names the source of our row, or the proof content matches. No identity matching between prove2.me and GitHub users. Credit goes to the source proof authors, else to the prove2.me solvers by their prove2.me usernames.

other-block-sensitivity.statement_form: SensitivityCampaign.AchievesExponent a: for every epsilon > 0 and every S >= 2 there is a total Boolean function f on Fin n bits with sensitivity(f) >= S and sensitivity(f)^(a-epsilon) <= blockSensitivity(f). Sensitivity is the largest number of single bit flips that change f, and block sensitivity is the largest number of disjoint nonempty bit sets that each change f at one input (Def_SensitivitySeparation, reviewed 2026-10-19). That is our statement: bs(f) >= s(f)^(alpha - o(1)) for a family of total Boolean functions with s(f) -> infinity.

integer-multiplication.statement_form: IntMul.KappaBound (1 / 2 ^ 182): one deterministic k-tape Turing machine (k >= 2: a read-only input tape, an output tape and k-2 work tapes, a fixed finite alphabet, Montanaro conventions) that for every n >= 1 and all x, y in {0,1}^n halts on input x#y with the output bin_2n(val(x) val(y)), in worst-case time at most c n (lg n)^(1 - kappa) for n >= n0, with lg n = max(ceil(log2 n), 1) and kappa = 2^-182. That is OpenAI Theorem 1 and our page statement (a Turing machine with a fixed finite alphabet and a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes). Definitions Def_IntMul_MultitapeModel pinned by hash; it has no instances, notations or axioms (reviewed 2026-10-19).

matrix-multiplication.statement_form: Not the campaign goals (matMulExp K < c, tensor rank over every field) but the goal OAI.MatrixMultiplication.complex_omega_le_nine_quarters: Arithmetic.omega C <= 9/4, where Arithmetic.omega is the infimum of the exponents tau such that for every epsilon > 0 one positive constant C bounds the cost of a correct division-free straight-line program for n x n complex matrix multiplication by C n^(tau + epsilon) at every size n. The definition file Def_OAI_MatrixMultiplication_Arithmetic_omega is openai/math adc7f12 lean/ComparatorChallenges/MatrixMultiplication.lean with its original declarations; after removing comments and blank lines it differs from our trusted challenge only in the import lines (specific Mathlib modules instead of import Mathlib) and in leaving out our three target theorems (reviewed 2026-10-19). The goal is our challenge theorem complex_omega_le_nine_quarters.
